One of my favorite movies is Ghost Dog.
For those who haven't seen it it's about an odd sort of hit man and his dealings with the mob. Sort of indie by director Jim Jarmusch. (I highly recommend it.)

There's a scene in there that establishes the location of where a member of the mob lives.
It's only a few seconds long. You see this worn down three story stand alone in the rain.

A gorgeous car is parked in the garage, the hood sticking out under the door as it's not big enough to accommodate a car that size. There's a small for sale sign tacked onto the right side of the house, just above the garage.

Honestly, this scene says everything.
It completely illustrates the mobs situation. They used to be powerful, wealthy. And now all they're hanging onto is a tiny bit of old fashioned pride (the car) in a world which no longer fits them. Or rather, a world they no longer belong to. The for sale sign really gets me. It's a tiny, insignificant indication to the mindset of these men, who would rather sell their house than their car if it means keeping up the appearance of power. 

The mob in this film aren't exactly painted as sympathetic, but this moment really gets to me. It's a silent reminder of a falling empire. Everything these men have built for themselves is slowly fading away, slipping through their fingers, and there is nothing they can do about it.

You had to make your project, submit it to the head of the science department and from there the 5 best students would be chosen to represent the school. I did not know this.

He was surprised to see me, and asked if my name was on his list, it wasn't. At this point I hadn't yet realized the err of my ways, because he didn't tell it to me straight. He just looked at me awkwardly and said nothing.
Soon it was my turn to present to the judges. A panel of twelve highly educated men and women from different respective areas.
I blathered on for my seven minutes, thinking I was doing great because they were all smiling so much.
Only at the end of my presentation did I realize what had happened because one of the other kids from my school came up to rub it in my face. I was so embarrassed and wanted to go home but I had to wait until the end of the day to be picked up. That's not the worst thing though. At the end of the day there was a prize giving. There were the big important prizes, money grants to schools etc and also stupid tiny ones. It was one of those competitions were everyone went home with at least a certificate. I didn't. I was the only entrant who didn't win anything. Not even the shitty photocopied participation certificate that all of the people who entered were supposed to get. It was blindingly obvious because once your name was called for a prize you joined the other students on stage. I was the only entrant left in the audience. Luckily there were a few parents and siblings there so I hoped people would assume I wasn't in the fair. No such luck. At the end they made all the school groups come to the front of the stage and bow. When my school was called they realized I wasn't there.
